description:
The surah that opens with the emphatic oath of the Divine One swearing by the looming day of **Resurrection**. It takes its name from verse 1, which mentions the Day of Resurrection. The surah dealing with the Day of Resurrection and man's denial of that Day. God's power is convincingly described in several vignettes (verse 3 ff., verse 26 ff. and verse 34 ff.). The third paragraph instructs the Prophet on appropriate reception of the revelation (verse 16 ff.), and thereby serves to emphasize that the Quran is indeed God's word.
The surah is also known as Day of Resurrection, The Rising

27.1: That is, by the angels of mercy and the angels of wrath present at the side of the dying person, as to which of them will take charge of him. Or those who are present by the side of the dying person say, 'Where is the medicine man?'

29.1: An idiom suggesting a time of great hardship, or, metaphorically, death throes.

translations.1: I swear by the Day of Resurrection!
translations.2: And I swear by the self-blaming soul!
translations.3:
Does man suppose
   that We shall not put together his bones?
translations.4:
Yes indeed,
 We are able to proportion [even] his fingertips!
translations.5: Rather man desires to go on living viciously.
translations.6: He asks, 'When is this day of resurrection?!'
translations.7: But when the eyes are dazzled,
translations.9: and the sun and the moon are brought together,
translations.10:
that day man will say,
  'Where is the escape?'
translations.11: No indeed! There is no refuge!
translations.12: That day the abode will be toward _your_ Lord.
translations.13:
That day man will be informed
 about what he has sent ahead and left behind.
translations.14: Rather man is a witness to himself,
translations.15: though he should offer his excuses.
translations.16: _Do not move your_ tongue with it to hasten it.
translations.17:
Indeed it is up to Us to put it together
   and to recite it.
translations.18: And when We have recited it, _follow_ its recitation.
translations.19: Then, its exposition indeed [also] lies with Us.
translations.20: No Indeed! Rather you love this transitory life
translations.22: Some faces will be fresh on that day,
translations.24: and some faces will be scowling on that day,
translations.25:
knowing that they will be dealt out
  a punishment breaking the spine.
translations.26:
No indeed!
  When the soul reaches up to the collar bones,
translations.27: and it is said, 'Who will take him up?'<{["F", 1]}>
translations.28: and he knows that it is the [time of] parting,
translations.29: and each shank clasps the other shank,<{["F", 1]}>
translations.30: that day he shall be driven toward _your_ Lord.
translations.31: He neither confirmed [the truth], nor prayed,
translations.33: and went swaggering to his family.
translations.34: So woe to you! Woe to you!
translations.35: Again, woe to you! Woe to you!
translations.36:
Does man suppose
   that he would be abandoned to futility?
translations.37: Was he not a drop of emitted semen?
translations.38:
Then he became a clinging mass;
 then He created [him] and proportioned [him],
translations.39:
and made of him the two sexes,
   the male and the female.
translations.40:
Is not such a one able
  to revive the dead?
